question: Should OpenClaw core bundle this 1Password SecretRef resolver that shells out to `op`, or should it stay as an external/ClawHub plugin until the security and dependency-graph policy is explicitly approved?
rationale: The implementation uses the existing plugin-managed SecretRef seam, but bundling a third-party secret-manager resolver changes core distribution, dependency/security review, runtime environment expectations, and credential execution trust boundaries.

options.title: Approve bundled resolver after secops review
options.body: Keep the core-bundled plugin direction, require current-head dependency approval, and repair the account/status redaction before merge.

options.title: Move to ClawHub/external plugin
options.body: Ask the contributor to publish the 1Password provider as a ClawHub or external plugin using the existing manifest SecretRef integration contract.

options.title: Keep manual exec docs only
options.body: Decline the bundled convenience plugin for now and rely on the existing documented manual exec provider path for operators who need 1Password.

recommendation.title: Approve bundled resolver after secops review
recommendation.body: Keep the core-bundled plugin direction, require current-head dependency approval, and repair the account/status redaction before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The central plugin-managed SecretRef provider seam and docs route through recent work attributed to @vincentkoc, and the decision needs that seam's owner plus secops review.
